title: Three pots, one plan
topic: Split your savings and automate them

steps.title: Three pots for your money
steps.body: Many people split their savings into three pots. Pot one is the safety net: a few months of costs, ready any day. Pot two is for goals in the next few years, like a trip or a new laptop. Pot three is money that can wait 10 years or more. If it stays in savings, [[inflation]] eats into it. A [[standing-order]] on payday fills the pots by itself.

stat.label: pots: safety net, goals, long term

steps.prompt: Match each pot with the money that belongs in it.
pairs: Moves money on payday by itself

steps.prompt: Why do people count an emergency fund in months of costs, not as a round amount?
options: The fund has to pay for life while an income is missing
steps.explanation: An [[emergency-fund]] replaces income for a while, so its size follows what life costs you each month.

steps.prompt: True or false: money kept in a savings account for 20 years keeps its value, because the balance never falls.
steps.explanation: False. Over 20 years, [[inflation]] can take a big bite when the interest is lower than the price rise. That is why long-term money often sits in its own pot.

scenes.title: Three pots
scenes.desc: A safety net, a goal pot and a long-term pot. A [[standing-order]] fills them, and the long-term pot is where [[inflation]] hurts most. The safety net is your [[emergency-fund]].
